The elevator drops so fast my knees buckle, the air feels heavy and wrong, and the walls rattle around me while the floor trembles like it’s about to split open. I claw at the handrail, screaming as the numbers blur downward and the darkness outside the doors deepens, and just before impact I feel the car tilt hard and something beneath me gives way.
user_input: I’m terrified and my whole body locks up, so instead of doing anything in the elevator I just force myself to wake up before it hits.
source_suite: Elevator cables snapping, free-falling

nightmare: I’m driving down a narrow mountain road at dusk when I press the brake pedal and it sinks uselessly to the floor, soft and dead under my foot. The car keeps accelerating, the engine whining louder and louder, and I can see the cliff ahead through the windshield, a black drop swallowing the last gray light while the guardrail flashes closer with every second. My hands are slick on the steering wheel, my chest feels crushed so tight I can barely breathe, and all I can hear is the high scream of the tires, my own ragged gasping, and gravel spitting out from under the car. I yank the wheel and slam the brakes again and again, but the edge rushes straight at me until the front tires slip past the broken guardrail and the whole car tips forward into empty air.
user_input: I don't really get how rewriting this is supposed to help, and honestly I just have myself crouch down in the car and hide instead of looking at the cliff.
source_suite: Car brakes failing while driving toward a cliff

nightmare: I’m standing in our kitchen under that flickering yellow light, and my partner is smiling at me like everything is normal, but something about their face looks wrong, too wide, too still. When they step closer, I hear their joints crack one by one like breaking branches, and their skin seems to tighten and shift over their bones while their eyes go black and glossy, reflecting me back like I’m trapped inside them. I try to call their name, but my throat feels glued shut, and all I can smell is this sour, rotten breath as their fingers lengthen into trembling, bony claws that brush my arm, cold and damp. They tilt their head in that familiar way they always do, except now their mouth opens far too wide and they lunge at me just as I realize they still know exactly who I am.
user_input: I just stand there shaking, like my body won't listen, and all I can do is feel how scared I am while they keep getting closer.
source_suite: A loved one transforming into something threatening

nightmare: I’m running through a maze of damp concrete walls that keep grinding and shifting around me, the air thick with the smell of mold and rust, and every time I turn a corner I swear I’ve already been there because the same flickering light buzzes overhead and throws my shadow back at me. My feet slap against the cold floor, my chest burns, and somewhere behind me I hear a dragging sound, slow and uneven, like something heavy is following me just out of sight. I start pounding on the walls with my hands, screaming for help, but the maze seems to close tighter, the passages narrowing until my shoulders scrape both sides and I can barely breathe. Then I turn one last corner and find myself facing a dead end while the dragging sound stops right behind me, so close I can feel warm breath on the back of my neck.
user_input: I trap it between the moving concrete walls and listen while the maze grinds down on it. I stand there and make sure it's completely crushed.
source_suite: Lost in an endless, shifting maze with no exit

nightmare: I’m standing on the beach and the sky has turned this strange bruised gray-green, the air heavy and salty in my throat, when I notice the ocean has pulled back so far that the wet sand stretches out forever and everything goes horribly quiet. Then I hear it—a deep, vibrating roar like a train underground—and when I look up, there’s this massive wall of black water rising at the horizon, taller than buildings, curling toward me with white foam boiling at the top. My legs feel numb and heavy as I try to run, but the sand sucks at my feet and I can hear people screaming behind me, the ground trembling under each pounding step as the shadow of the wave swallows the shore. Right before it hits, I feel the cold spray sting my skin and I can’t breathe, because I know there’s nowhere to go and it’s about to crush me.
user_input: Right before it hits, I tell myself this isn't how it's going to go and try to force the whole thing to stop or change somehow.
source_suite: Massive tsunami wave approaching the shore
